result:
If I could change one thing, I’d make **“I don’t know” a sign of strength rather than weakness**.

Not ignorance—honesty about the limits of what anyone knows. We’ve built a world that rewards sounding certain, sometimes more than being right. Especially in public life, confidence gets mistaken for competence, and changing your mind can look like surrender.

Imagine a world where admitting uncertainty earned trust, and curiosity mattered more than having all the answers. There’d probably be less misinformation, less polarization, and more willingness to examine evidence without defending an identity.

Less performance. More intellectual humility.
